incarnation: Aliens (1986) - Hadley's Hope atmosphere processor, LV-426
visualFidelity: pending; existing sprites and scenery not certified as 1:1
sourceFacts: Ripley frees Newt from the hive and escapes the atmosphere processor with her.
The Queen survives the hive escape and appears aboard the Sulaco later.
The power-loader confrontation belongs to the Sulaco cargo lock, not the processor hive.
implemented: Spatial rescue marker becomes usable when the existing Queen wave arrives.
Living hero must reach Newt within the authored interaction radius and free her.
Newt accompanies one carrier; she has no HP, enemy entry or damageable combat entity.
Living carrier must reach the separate exit marker and explicitly evacuate.
Queen normal and external damage remains nonlethal; fixed external HP loss preserves its amount and optional shield absorption.
Queen cannot provide generic boss-kill or ringout victory.
Carrier loss defeats the rescue mission, including with another living hero at the exit.
AutoBattle crosses the original waves and physically travels between rescue and exit, retaining actor statistics.
Wrong incarnation/mode/boss/roster, custom flags and different scenes preserve generic combat.

Only source-hive Ripley Aliens receives a runtime loadout copy: Hive Cover, M41A grenade launcher special, directional pulse-rifle range and a short-range incinerator. Other incarnations/scenes and the source hero database remain unchanged.
gameAdaptations: Existing three combat waves before the Queen are retained and do not recreate the film editing or chronology.
2D platforms, marker coordinates, interaction radius, instantaneous rescue action and abbreviated return route are game choices.
One living carrier and carrier-loss defeat are game rules. The child is neither displayed as a damageable combatant nor subject to an HP gauge.
Nonlethal Queen HP floor and fall repositioning preserve the source outcome through a game-specific combat model.

Nest, lifts, stairs and landing platform are compressed into one arena. No exact film geometry, lift timing, egg-sac burn sequence, facehugger rescue choreography or full processor destruction is claimed.

The Sulaco power-loader finale is still separate and unimplemented. Only the source-hive Ripley Aliens runtime exchanges power-loader actions for hive cover and an M41A grenade. Defensive reduction, damage, ranges, hit limits, local projectile/flame feedback and special charge remain game adaptations, not film measurements or certified prop art.

sources.role: Official distributor; film identity, year, director and cast. Does not substantiate detailed rescue rules.
James Cameron screenplay hosted by IMSDb, scenes 173–185 and later Sulaco cargo-lock scenes. Draft evidence: details differ from the released film.
Secondary plot summary corroborating Newt rescue, processor evacuation and separate Sulaco Queen confrontation.
